messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: meaning of error in RStan?
parts:
[to stan-dev]

I am pretty sure this is doable in R because it is not to hard to evaluate the elements of a named vector, such as

inits <- c(betacount = 3, alpha = 1.0)

and so forth. I guess you could do the same kind of thing in command-line Stan. I kind of would like to have an optional init{} block in the .stan file but I guess we first need random sampling for that to be useful.

Ben

On Wed, Nov 7, 2012 at 3:02 PM, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com> wrote:
cced Ben as he was asking about partially specifying inits. 

Regarding the error message, the way I can think of is to catch the exception thrown from the dump reader when I do the initialization and then throw a new message.  I think you would have the same problem if using Stan on command line.  So then I am not sure it is a good idea. 

--
Jiqiang 


On Wed, Nov 7, 2012 at 2:44 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
On 11/7/12 1:20 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
Did you provide your own inits?  In that case, betacount might be not specified in your inits.

Thanks -- adding full inits solved the problem.

Is there a way to make the message more specific to let the
user know the problem was in inits?

I'm thinking it'd be nice if we could have partial inits.
I'll think about how to do it in Stan and then hopefully
we can work it into RStan.

- Bob

Shame on me for not doing that the first time around!

I just wrapped the init in a try/catch that displays
a better error when the initialization throws an exception.

For non-existent init files:

~/stan>src/models/basic_estimators/normal_truncated --init=foojazz
--data=src/models/basic_estimators/normal_truncated.Rdata
Error during user-specified initialization:
Specified init file does not exist: foojazz

and for badly formatted ones:

~/stan>src/models/basic_estimators/normal_truncated --init=/Users/carp/temp2/init.R
--data=src/models/basic_estimators/normal_truncated.Rdata

variable mu missing
~/stan>


I could instead have the generated model code throw
a better exception by putting the try/catch there. If
that'd be easier for you (Jiqiang), I can do that.

Reading partial inits is a bit harder code-wise because
of how the I/O is currently written. But one we should
be able to code through.

- Bob

One reason I found so far is that in the stanc (from command line Stan)-generated cpp code for a model,

I have 

stan::io::reader<var> in__(params_r__,params_i__);
vector<var> y;

while in RStan, it is 

stan::io::read<double> in__(params_r__,params_i__);
vector<double> y;

So I guess I am close to find the reason. 

--
Jiqiang

parts:
On 11/12/12 8:41 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> One reason I found so far is that in the stanc (from command line Stan)-generated cpp code for a model,
>

>
> stan::io::reader<var> in__(params_r__,params_i__);
> vector<var> y;
>
> while in RStan, it is
>
> stan::io::read<double> in__(params_r__,params_i__);
> vector<double> y;
>
> So I guess I am close to find the reason.

That's definitely a problem, because the compiler is taking
params_r__ to be var:
> file34e6643d6d84.cpp:99: error: no matching function for call to

> ï¿½stan::io::reader<double>::reader(std::vector<stan::agrad::var, std::allocator<stan::agrad::var> >&,
> std::vector<int, std::allocator<int> >&)ï¿½

If the input is vector<var>, the class needs to be
specified as reader<var>. What I'm not clear on is how
this could've worked before the change I just made.

I added a function to the generate model with signature:

double log_prob(std::vector<double>&, std::vector<int>&);

to the existing:

var log_prob(std::vector<var>&, std::vector<int>&);

The double-based function will make it more efficient to just evaluate
the log probability function. For now, it'll only
speed up finite difference calcs, but in the future, it'll help
define new samplers that don't need gradients.

- Bob
